newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Albanian minister says June poll still planned.
newsitem.headline: Albanian minister says June poll still planned.

text.p: Albanian Foreign Minister Arjan Starova said on Monday a general election would be held as promised on June 29 because the government was regaining control in the rebel south.
Starova, speaking to reporters after talks with Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel, said rebel committees holding some towns in the south were the only obstacle to the elections.
"We will have elections in June... Some committees remain in the south, but there are not as many as before," Starova said, adding nearly half of the south was now back in government control.

The situation in Albania, thrown into chaos after the collapse of bogus investment schemes, had largely improved with public order restored in most parts of the country, said Starova, a member of the centre-left Social Democratic Union.

Rebel committees refuse to give up as long as President Sali Berisha remains in power. Berisha's rightist Democrats, however, have demanded that the committees lay down their arms before any elections take place.

An all-party unity government was set up last month in the midst of widespread violence and looting after an agreement to hold elections in June, just a year after parliamentary polls widely regarded as flawed.
